rev4_retraction.what_was_claimed: That ~22 workers were deleted on 2026-09-11 between 09:19Z and 16:45Z, inferred from per-name HTTP status in fleet_probe_log flipping 200 to 404.
rev4_retraction.line_1_liveness: cloud_ops_events grouped by job shows workers writing to D1 TODAY: qnfo-pipeline-ops n=978 last 2026-09-13T14:31:19.094Z; qnfo-fleet-advisor n=376 last 2026-09-13T14:21:14.547Z; qnfo-register-guard n=7 last 2026-09-13T04:30:44.175Z. A deleted worker cannot write.
rev4_retraction.line_2_transport: The probed URL is IDENTICAL in both outcomes: https://<name>.q08.workers.dev/health. Only the transport differs. qnfo-pipeline-ops: transport=http ok=1 status=200 n=13 last 2026-09-10T12:21:46; transport=cf-api-list ok=1 status=200 n=131 last 2026-09-11T16:30:50; transport=http ok=0 status=404 n=68 last 2026-09-12T09:15:45. Same shape for qnfo-fleet-advisor, qnfo-register-guard, qnfo-auditor, fleet-executor.
rev4_retraction.corrected_cause: The 404s began when the dashboard switched probe transport from cf-api-list to http. The 404 is the documented SVC-BINDING-1 artifact: same-account workers.dev fetches return 404 at the edge from inside a Worker.

corrected_liveness_method.rule: Liveness CANNOT be measured from probe status - a 404 conflates 'worker gone' with 'transport cannot reach it'. Liveness must be measured from D1 writes by the worker itself (cloud_ops_events.job, or the worker's own tables).
corrected_liveness_method.limitation: Workers that never write cloud_ops_events yield no signal by this method and must be reported UNDETERMINED, not classified from probe data.
